findings.trace: The local validator returns Result<(), DesignError> and ParametricParameters for its listed bounds, including only an upper bound 11 on section_break. The field documents zero as unsplit. Shape validation first calls the local validator and then requires Tassets kind; a mismatch returns the same typed design error. Parent validation exposes Result<(), GenerateError>, propagates shape errors via ?, and converts the same design error with .into() if break >= lame_count. GenerateError::Design has #[from] DesignError; DesignError::ParametricParameters has its own generic armor-shape error annotation. No string-valued parameter or return exists in the exact local validator body.
findings.limits: The ordering of shape, fluting, parent bounds and break checks matters; this read does not prove general deserialization admission, all call sites, native outcomes, or a player-visible error.

findings.status: bounded source observation, no newly asserted defect
findings.trace: Ordinary Tassets new() creates four lames with ordinary nonwrapped Tassets shape. Independently replacing its shape with default WrappedTassets preserves default break 6; local controls and other parent defaults pass the shown checks, then 6 >= 4 fails the parent break/count check. This is static reasoning about the publicly representable aggregate, not an executed fixture or an established selected-user interaction. The selected editor calls tasset_construction then the wrapped controls, which cap the break at count.saturating_sub(1); the editor label explicitly offers zero as unsplit. Warmup sets eight lames before choosing default wrapped break 6. The shown GPU entry validates the parent before course division; nothing here proves its native operation.

The public garment validator returns that shared GenerateError for invalid wrapped-tasset designs, including the conceptual break-6/count-4 aggregate above. If that error is formatted through its annotated Display implementation, the bracer-specific prefix describes a tasset failure incorrectly; the underlying ParametricParameters annotation says armor shape parameters. This concern belongs to the outer text boundary and does not contradict the no-string local-validator observation.
